tool.name: OGSTools msh2vtu
tool.description: Convert a Gmsh mesh to VTU submeshes
tool.command: @SET_OGS_BIN_PATH@ && mkdir -p out && ln -s '$input_file' input_file.msh && msh2vtu input_file.msh --output_path out --dim $dim $delz $swapxy $reindex $ascii

param.label: Dimensionality of the submeshes to extract
param.help: Cells of this dimension are collected into the domain mesh, one dimension less into the physical group meshes.

param.name: delz
param.label: Set the z-coordinate to 0
param.help: Useful for 2D meshes that are not located in the xy-plane.

param.name: reindex
param.label: Renumber material IDs
param.help: Renumber the material IDs of the domain mesh so that they start at zero.

param.name: ascii
param.label: Save in ASCII format
param.help: By default the mesh data is appended as binary data.

tool.help:
**Overview**
`msh2vtu` converts a Gmsh mesh (`.msh`) into a set of VTU meshes ready for use with OpenGeoSys. The domain mesh holds all cells matching the requested dimensionality, and one submesh is written for each physical group of the input mesh, named after that group. Two-dimensional input meshes additionally get one submesh per physical group of one dimension less (i.e. the boundaries).
Supported element types:
- lines (linear and quadratic) in 1D - triangles and quadrilaterals (linear and quadratic) in 2D - tetrahedra and hexahedra (linear and quadratic) in 3D
**Inputs**
- **Input Gmsh mesh**: the `.msh` file to convert. - **Dimensionality**: dimension of the domain mesh, 1, 2 or 3. The physical group submeshes have either the same dimension (subdomains) or one dimension less (boundaries), depending on the dimension of the group in the `.msh` file. - **Set the z-coordinate to 0**: flatten a 2D mesh that does not lie in the xy-plane. - **Swap the x- and y-coordinates**: exchange the first two coordinates. - **Renumber material IDs**: renumber the material IDs of the domain mesh starting at zero. - **Save in ASCII format**: write the mesh data as ASCII instead of appending binary data.
**Outputs**
A collection of VTU meshes: the `domain` dataset holds the bulk mesh, one further dataset is created per physical group and named after that group.
